- If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) or oscillating, model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is near support.
- After sharp spikes (e.g., >70.00), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias or add lagged mean reversion term.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early 30d forecasts — if true outcome deviates >5% from 10d moving average, adjust forecast toward that average.
- When sentiment flips from bullish to bearish (or vice versa), model lags by 1–3 days; add 1–3 day lagged sentiment weight to forecast adjustment.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a peak, model often fails to recognize it — apply downward correction with sentiment decay factor (e.g., 0.8 per day if sentiment <0.33).
